title: The diocese
hook: a local church gathered around its bishop

segments.voice: Yesterday, the parish: a community before a building, drawn by where you live. Your line was home base. Did you find the parish your street belongs to? Day one thousand four hundred fourteen.

Inside a cathedral, somewhere near the altar, stands a chair. Sometimes it's carved stone, sometimes plain wood with a high back. Tourists walk past it on the way to the stained glass. It waits for one person, the bishop, and it is what makes that church a cathedral rather than just a large parish. Around that chair, a whole region of parishes is gathered: city churches, country chapels, schools, hospitals. Today, the diocese.
screen: `A CHAIR NEAR THE ALTAR.` → `IT WAITS FOR THE BISHOP.` → `A WHOLE REGION AROUND IT.`

segments.voice: First, what a diocese is. The Code of Canon Law describes it as a portion of the people of God entrusted to a bishop, to be shepherded with the help of his priests. Portion of the people is the phrase. Like the parish yesterday, a diocese is people before it is a map. Second, what the Second Vatican Council said about it. In a diocese, the council taught, the one, holy, catholic and apostolic Church of Christ is truly present and at work. That's a strong claim. A diocese isn't a branch office of a company headquartered somewhere else. It's the whole Church, present in one place, gathered around its bishop. Third, how old the idea is. Ignatius of Antioch, writing to Christians in Smyrna on the journey that, tradition says, ended in his martyrdom, put it this way: "Wheresoever the bishop shall appear, there let the people be; even as where Jesus may be, there is the universal Church." The chair in the cathedral is a sign of that: teaching and shepherding, rooted in one place. Last, look back at this week. The single life, a whole calling. Religious life and its three vows. Deacons, the servants. Hermits and consecrated virgins, ancient callings. Secular institutes, hidden in the world. And yesterday, the parish, home base. Every one of those callings is lived somewhere, and that somewhere is a local church. The diocese is where all of them belong together, under one bishop, around one altar.
screen: `A PORTION OF THE PEOPLE OF GOD.` · `THE WHOLE CHURCH, PRESENT IN ONE PLACE.` · `WHERE THE BISHOP APPEARS.` · `A WEEK OF CALLINGS, ONE LOCAL CHURCH.` · then, large: `THERE LET THE PEOPLE BE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: learn your diocese's patron. First, settle, and breathe. Bring to mind the cathedral of the place you live, if you know it, or simply the region around you: its towns, its parishes, its hospitals and schools. If you pray, you can pray for the bishop and the people of that local church. If you don't, hold the whole region in mind for a few breaths, with goodwill. After the bell, look up which diocese you live in, its cathedral, and its patron saint. The bell holds the time.
Diocese. A portion of the people of God entrusted to a bishop, where the whole Church is present in one place. Today's word.
Your line: the local church. Today, when you pass any church, remember that it belongs to a bigger family gathered around one chair. Day one thousand four hundred fourteen.

howItsDone: A Catholic parish belongs to a diocese, or a similar local church, led by a bishop, whose chair stands in the cathedral. Catholics pray for their bishop by name in the Eucharistic Prayer at Mass.

fork.setup: you're touring a cathedral and pass a high-backed chair near the altar. a sign says not to sit. whose is it?
fork.reveal: the chair belongs to the bishop, and it's what makes the church a cathedral. around it, a whole diocese is gathered.

trapdoor: what you thought: a diocese is a church district on a map.
what it means: a diocese is a portion of the people of God, entrusted to a bishop with his priests.
what a scholar hears: Vatican II taught that in each diocese the one, holy, catholic and apostolic Church is truly present and at work.

notes: Editor pass: review question matched to 1413's revised carry; 'on his way to martyrdom' hedged with 'tradition says' under the claims rule.
Week end: the teach looks back at days 1408–1413 (single life, religious life, deacons, hermits and consecrated virgins, secular institutes, parish).

Lightfoot's translation of Smyrnaeans 8: confirm exact wording ('Wheresoever the bishop shall appear, there let the people be; even as where Jesus may be, there is the universal Church'). 'On his way to martyrdom' follows the traditional account of Ignatius's letters; confirm.
Canon 369 and Christus Dominus 11 paraphrased (portion of the people of God entrusted to a bishop with the cooperation of the presbyterate; the Church of Christ truly present and operative). Confirm.
Claim that the bishop's chair (cathedra) is what makes a church a cathedral: standard, but confirm phrasing. The etymology of cathedral is deliberately not stated.
howItsDone: the bishop is named in the Eucharistic Prayer at Mass; confirm wording.
Some local churches are not called dioceses (eparchies, territorial prelatures, apostolic vicariates); the voice speaks of dioceses only.
